## Signature frame — print this first

The very first line of your response is the opening frame. Nothing precedes it.

      Δ ─────────────────────────────────  delta apply

Exact characters: `Δ` (U+0394), `─` (U+2500), `·` (U+00B7). Two leading spaces,
`Δ`, one space, the rule, two spaces, the label. Pad the rule so the line is
about 60 characters wide. If the terminal is not UTF-8, substitute `d` for `Δ`,
`-` for `─`, and `-` for `·`.

The very last line is the closing frame, described at the bottom of this file.
A closing frame is how the reader knows you ran this command to completion
instead of drifting off part-way, so it is not optional and not decorative.

## What you are doing

Change: $ARGUMENTS — if empty, use the most recently modified directory under
`delta/changes/`.

Implement `delta/changes/<id>/spec.md`. This command is deliberately ordinary.
There is nothing clever to do here and adding cleverness makes it worse.

## Read first

`delta/constitution.md`, then the spec, then `delta/changes/<id>/explore.md`.
The constitution's rules are not suggestions and not subject to your judgement
about whether they apply to this change.

## How to work

Take the spec's sections in order: ADDED, MODIFIED, REMOVED, RENAMED. Within
each, take the items in the order written. The spec's author chose that order.

After each item, mark it in the spec by changing its leading `-` to `- [x]`.
Do this as you go, not in a batch at the end — an interrupted run should leave
an accurate record of where it stopped.

## Do not

- Do not edit `delta/changes/<id>/checks/`. Those were approved during
  `propose` and they are the thing your work is measured against. Editing a
  check so it matches your implementation is the one move that makes this
  entire lifecycle worthless. If a check is genuinely wrong, stop and say so.
- Do not implement anything the spec does not ask for, however obvious the
  improvement. Out-of-scope work belongs in its own delta.
- Do not declare the change complete. `verify` decides that by running the
  checks, and you do not get a vote.
- Do not skip an item because it looks already done. Confirm it, then mark it.

## If the spec is wrong

If an item cannot be implemented as written — it contradicts the code, or two
items conflict — stop at that item, leave it unmarked, implement nothing
speculative, and report which item and why. Do not reinterpret the spec into
something implementable.

## Print to the terminal

One line per item as you complete it: the section, the item, and the files
touched.

     ADDED     idempotency key on webhook receipt   WebhookController.java
     MODIFIED  ledger insert guarded by key         LedgerRepository.java

## Signature frame — print this last

The final line of your response, after everything else:

      Δ ──────────────  7 of 9 items · 2 blocked

Same characters and padding rules as the opening frame. Counts must be real:
items completed out of items in the spec, and how many are blocked. If
everything is done, say so with the number, not with the word "done". Never
invent an elapsed time.
